1. A method (60), implemented by a packet forwarding circuit (18) disposed between a control server (14) and an actuator (17), for controlling the actuator, the method comprising:
Receiving (62), from the control server, trajectory information (20) for controlling the actuator, wherein the trajectory information defines a sequence target points (32) along a trajectory (30) to be followed by the actuator;
receiving (64), from the actuator, a status message (22) comprising status information about the actuator;
generating (70) a command message (24) to control the actuator based on the status information and the received trajectory information; and
sending (78) the command message to the actuator.
2. The method of claim 1 further comprising storing the trajectory information received from the control server in a trajectory table (40) in memory (212) of the packet forwarding circuit.
3. The method of any of claims 1 and 2 wherein the trajectory information received from the control server comprises all the target points in the trajectory to be followed by the actuator.
4. The method of any of claims 1 and 2 wherein the trajectory information received from the control server comprises a subset of less than all the target points in the trajectory to be followed by the actuator for a predetermined period of time.
5. The method of any of claims 1-5 further comprising storing (104) an actuator state in the one or more registers at the packet forwarding circuit, wherein the one or more registers are accessible only to the packet forwarding circuit.
6. The method of any of claims 1-5 wherein the actuator state defines one or both of position information and velocity information for the actuator.
7. The method of any of claims 1-6 wherein generating the command message comprises converting (82) the status message to the command message.
8. The method of any of claims 1-7 wherein the status message and the command message comprise respective headers, and wherein converting the status message comprises:
removing (84) the status message header from the status message;
modifying (86) a destination address of the status message to be an address of the actuator;
adding (88) the command message header to the command message; and
initializing (90) the command message header.
9. The method of any of claims 1-8 generating the command message further comprises calculating (120) a velocity vector for the actuator, wherein the velocity vector defines a velocity at which the actuator is to move a joint of a robotic arm (16) from a first position defined by a current target point in the sequence to a second position defined by a next target point in the sequence.
10. The method of claim 9 wherein calculating a velocity vector comprises:
determining (122) a time duration for the actuator, wherein the time duration defines an amount of time that the actuator has to move the joint from the first position to the second position; and
initializing (128) a set of temporary variables associated with the actuator responsive to determining (126) that the time duration has not yet been initialized.
11. The method of any of claims 9-10 wherein calculating a velocity vector further comprises determining whether the joint moved by the actuator has reached the first position based on a comparison (126) of a current time to the time duration.
12. The method of any of claims 9-11 further comprising:
replacing (132) information in the current target point in the sequence with information from the next target point in the sequence responsive to determining (130) that the actuator has finished moving the joint to the first position; and
loading (134) the current target point in the sequence responsive to determining (134) that
the actuator has not yet finished moving the joint to the first position.
13. The method of any of claims 9-12 further comprising updating (136) the trajectory table at the packet forwarding circuit to include information associated with the current target point.
14. The method of any of claims 9-13 wherein updating a trajectory table at the packet forwarding circuit comprises, responsive to determining (138) that the actuator has finished moving the device to the first position, or that the time duration was initialized, updating (142) the time duration of the next target point in the sequence by adding (140) the time duration of the next target point in the sequence to the time duration of the current target point in the sequence.
15. The method of claim 14 wherein each target point in the sequence comprises a unique target id that identifies the target point, and wherein updating the trajectory table further comprises updating (144) the target id of the next target point in the sequence at the packet forwarding circuit.
16. The method of any of claims 9-15 wherein calculating a velocity vector for the actuator comprises:
obtaining (148) one or both of the velocity information and the position information from the current target point; and
calculating (150) the velocity vector for the actuator based on the one or both of the velocity information and the position information.
17. The method of any of claims 1-16 further comprising encoding (152) the velocity vector into the command header of the command message.
18. The method of any of the preceding claims wherein each target point defines a target id, timing information, and a sequence of one or both of velocity values and position values along a continuous trajectory curve.
19. The method of any of the preceding claims wherein the actuator is configured to receive a periodic control signal.
20. The method of any of the preceding claims wherein the actuator is associated with a robotic arm.
21. The method of any of the preceding claims wherein the actuator is configured to control a motor that moves the robotic arm.
22. The method of claim 21 wherein the actuator is configured to move the robotic arm between two positions.
23. The method of claim 21 wherein the actuator is configured to control a velocity at which the robotic arm moves between two positions.
24. The method of any of the preceding claims further comprising the packet forwarding circuit controlling a plurality of actuators.
25. The method of claim 24 wherein each actuator is identified using a device id stored in the trajectory table at the packet forwarding circuit.
26. The method of any of the preceding claims wherein the packet forwarding circuit is a programmable switch.
27. The method of any of the preceding claims wherein the packet forwarding circuit is a router.
28. The method of claim 1 wherein generating a command message comprises:
receiving (184) a dummy command message from a command message generator device (170); and
modifying (198) the dummy command message based on the trajectory information and the
status information.
29. A packet forwarding circuit (18) disposed between a control server (14) and one or more actuators (17), the packet forwarding circuit comprising:
communications circuitry (214) configured to communicate with both the control server and
the one or more actuators; and
processing circuitry (210) operatively connected to the communications circuitry and configured to perform any of the embodiments 1-28.
30. A non-transitory computer-readable medium (212) storing a computer program (216) thereon, the computer program comprising instructions that, when executed by processing circuitry (210) of a packet forwarding circuit (18) disposed between a control server (14) and one or more actuators (17), causes the packet forwarding circuit to perform any of the embodiments 1-28.
31. A computer program (216) comprising executable instructions that, when executed by processing circuitry (210) of a packet forwarding circuit (18) disposed between a control server (14) and one or more actuators (17), causes the packet forwarding circuit to perform any of the embodiments 1-28.
